===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|id=Q188691|:inh|enm:web<id:woven fabric>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|web}}, {{m|enm|webbe}}, from {{inh|en|ang|webb}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*wabi}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*wabją|t=web}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*webaną|t=to weave}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*webʰ-|t=to braid, weave}}.
{{col-top|2-|cog}}
Cognate with {{cog|sco|wab|t=web}}, {{cog|frr|wääb|t=web}}, {{cog|stq|Wäb|t=web}}, {{cog|fy,nl|web|t=web}}, {{cog|da|væv|t=web}}, {{cog|fo|vevur|t=web}}, {{cog|is|vefur|t=web}}, {{cog|nb,nn|vev|t=web}}, {{cog|sv|väv|t=web}}; also {{cog|kw|goghi|t=wasps}}, {{cog|ga|foich}}, {{m|ga|foiche}}, {{m|ga|puch|t=wasp}}, {{cog|cy|gwchi|t=drone}}, {{cog|la|vespa|t=wasp}}, {{cog|grc|ὑφή|t=web}}, {{m|grc|ὑφαίνω|t=to weave}} (whence {{cog|el|ανυφαίνω}}, {{m|el|υφαίνω|t=to weave}}), {{cog|sq|vej|t=to weave}}, {{cog|lv|lapsene|t=wasp}}, {{cog|lt|vapsvà|t=wasp}}, {{cog|prg|wobse|t=wasp}}, {{cog|be|аса́|t=wasp}}, {{cog|bg,mk,ru,uk|оса́|t=wasp}}, {{cog|cs|vosa|t=wasp}}, {{cog|pl,sk,sl|osa|t=wasp}}, {{cog|sh|о̀са}}, {{m|sh|òsa|t=wasp}}, {{cog|hy|մոզ|t=a kind of fly that bites horses and cattle}}, {{cog|kmr|moz|t=hornet; wasp}}, {{cog|fa|بافتن|tr=bâftan|t=to weave}}, {{cog|xto|wäp-|t=to weave}}, {{cog|txb|wāp-|t=to weave}}, {{cog|sa|उभ्नाति|t=to hurt, kill; to cover; fill}}.
{{col-bottom}}

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/wɛb/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-web.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɛb|s=1}}

===Noun===
{{wikidata lexeme|L12284}}
{{en-noun}}

# {{senseid|en|spiderweb}} The [[silk]]en structure which a [[spider]] builds using silk secreted from the [[spinneret]]s at the [[caudal]] tip of its abdomen; a [[spiderweb]].
#: {{syn|en|cobweb|spiderweb}}
#: {{ux|en|The sunlight glistened in the dew on the '''web'''.}}
## {{lb|en|zoology}} Any of several similar materials, such as that created by [[tent caterpillar]]s.
# {{lb|en|by extension}} Any [[interconnect]]ed [[set]] of [[person]]s, [[place]]s, or [[thing]]s, which, when [[diagram]]med, [[resemble]]s a [[spider]]'s web.
#: {{syn|en|spiderweb}}
#: {{hypo|en|food web}}
#* {{RQ:Irving Columbus|volume=I|chapter=Birth, Parentage, and Education of Columbus|page=3|passage=The time of his birth, his birth-place, his parentage, are all involved in obscurity; and such has been the perplexing ingenuity of commentators, that it is difficult to extricate the truth from the '''web''' of conjectures with which it is interwoven.}}
#* {{RQ:Hawthorne Snow-Image|story=Main-Street|page=96|passage=[T]he blame must rest on the sombre spirit of our forefathers, who wove their '''web''' of life with hardly a single thread of rose-color or gold, and not on me, who have a tropic-love of sunshine, and would gladly gild all the world with it, if I knew where to find so much.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|date=14 February 2018|author=Dan Shive|title=El Goonish Shive|section=Comic for Wednesday, Feb 14, 2018|sectionurl=https://www.egscomics.com/comic/2018-02-14|format=webcomic|text="''But THAT!  Was the OLDEN TIMES!''  A ''massive, worldwide '''web''''' of ''global information'' has ''ENTANGLED THE WORLD!''<!-- judging from the background graphics in that panel and from the "entangled" metaphor, Tedd ''is'' actually using "web" in the "interconnected set of whatevs" sense here, rather than the specific "internet" sense -->  People in ''Beijing'' can read about a magical incident in Moperville in ''seconds,'' and have ''video'' of it in ''minutes!''"}}
## {{lb|en|figurative}} A [[scheme]].
##: {{co|en|'''web''' of lies}}
##: {{syn|en|cobweb|intrigue}}
##: {{ux|en|She got lost in a '''web''' of international intrigue.}}
## {{lb|en|Internet}} The [[Internet]]; the [[World Wide Web]].
## {{lb|en|dated|US|radio|television}} A [[major]] [[broadcasting]] [[network]].
##* {{quote-journal|en|year=1950|journal=Billboard|volume=62|issue=43|page=9
|passage={{...}} the first big move toward a contract for television performers was made Friday (20) when the '''webs''' agreed to pay them according to the length of the show. {{...}} Altho the major TV '''webs''' — NBC and CBS — may fall in line soon, an agreement may possibly be held up by the opposition of DuMont {{...}}}}
##* {{quote-journal|en|year=1955|journal=Billboard|page=5
|passage=ABC-TV this week put into effect its long anticipated plans to move into daytime programming in a bigger way by opening up its 4-5 across-the-board strip. The '''web''' is using its "Mickey Mouse Club," which is stoutly anchored in the 5-6 p.m. slot, as a backing up point for its afternoon expansion.}}
# A latticed or woven structure.
#: {{near-syn|en|webbing}}
#: {{ux|en|The gazebo’s roof was a '''web''' made of thin strips of wood.}}
## {{senseid|en|baseball}} {{lb|en|baseball}} The part of a baseball mitt between the forefinger and thumb, the [[webbing]].
##: {{ux|en|He caught the ball in the '''web'''.}}
## {{lb|en|dated}} A [[band]] of [[webbing]] used to [[regulate]] the [[extension]] of the [[hood]] of a [[carriage]].
# ''Senses related to an invented narrative''
## {{lb|en|usually with "spin", "weave", or similar verbs}} A [[tall tale]] with more [[complexity]] than a [[myth]] or [[legend]].
##: {{syn|en|yarn}}
##: {{ux|en|Careful—she knows how to spin a good '''web''', but don't lean too hard on what she says.}}
##: {{ux|en|a tangled '''web''' of deception}}
## A [[plot]] or [[scheme]].
# Any of several components that connect other components.
## The interconnection between [[flange]]s in structural members, increasing the effective [[lever arm]] and so the load capacity of the member.
## {{senseid|en|rail section}} {{lb|en|rail transport}} The thinner vertical section of a railway [[rail]] between the top ([[head]]) and bottom ([[foot]]) of the rail.
##: {{cot|en|head|foot}}
## {{lb|en|anatomy}} A fold of [[tissue]] connecting the toes of certain birds or of other animals.
### The abnormal [[webbing]] sometimes present between the fingers or toes in humans.
## {{lb|en|architecture}} A section of a [[groin vault]], separated by [[rib]]s. {{rfc-sense|en}}
# A thin metal sheet, plate, or strip, as of lead.
## {{lb|en|manufacturing}} A continuous strip of material carried by rollers during processing.
## {{lb|en|lithography}} A long sheet of paper which is fed from a roll into a printing press, as opposed to individual sheets of paper.
## The blade of a [[saw]].
## The thin, sharp part of a [[colter]].
## The [[bit]] of a [[key]].
# {{senseid|en|glass}} {{lb|en|glassblowing|obsolete}} A seventeenth-century unit of [[Rhenish]] glass containing 60 [[bunch#English: glass|bunches]].
#: {{syn|en|way|id=glass}}
#* {{RQ:Tasso Fairfax Godfrey of Bulloigne|book=10|stanza=26|page=184|passage={{...}} And there with ſtately pompe by heapes they wend, / And Chriſtians ſlaine rolle vp in '''webs''' of lead {{...}}}}
## The [[blade]] of a [[sword]].
##* {{RQ:Tasso Fairfax Godfrey of Bulloigne|book=2|stanza=93|page=38|passage=''Argant'' a ſword, whereof the '''web''' was ſteele, / Pommell, rich ſtone ; hilts, gold, approu’d by tuch, / With rareſt workmanſhip all forged weele, / The curious art exceld the ſubſtance much.}}
# {{lb|en|ornithology}} The series of [[barb]]s implanted on each side of the [[shaft]] of a [[feather]], whether stiff and united together by [[barbule]]s, as in ordinary feathers, or soft and separate, as in downy feathers.
# {{lb|en|medicine|archaic}} A [[cataract]] of the [[eye]].
#: {{syn|en|pin and web|web and pin}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} Woven [[cloth]] or [[material]].
## {{lb|en|obsolete}} A piece of cloth or [[fabric]], as off the [[loom]] or being removed from a loom.

===Verb===
{{wikidata lexeme|L333484}}
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To construct or form a web.
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To cover with a web or network.
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=1853-06-21|author=R. C. Stone|title=A New Insect|editor=Simon Brown|journal=The New England Farmer|volume=V|location=Boston|publisher=Raynolds & Nourse|page=362|pageurl=https://books.google.com/books?id=2hY4AQAAMAAJ&pg=PA362&lpg=PA362|passage=The canker worm has no shelter upon the tree, but lies out upon the leaf or branch ; this forms itself a house by '''webbing''' the corner of a leaf, into which it retreats on the first appearance of danger{{...}}}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1895|title=Has Gold Risen?|journal=[[w:The Forum (defunct magazine)|The Forum]]|volume=XVIII|location=New York|publisher=The Forum Publishing Co.|page=577|pageurl=https://archive.org/stream/theforum18newy#page/577|passage=In the meantime continents were being ribbed with railways, the atmosphere was being '''webbed''' with telegraph wires connecting every important commercial centre{{...}}}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[ensnare]] or [[entangle]].
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To provide with a web.
# {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To [[weave]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1511–12|chapter=An Act agaynst deceyptfull making of Wollen Cloth|title=The Statures of the Realm|volume=III|location=London|publisher=Dawsons of Pall Mall|year_published=1963|page=28|pageurl=https://books.google.com/books?id=B7o4AQAAMAAJ&pg=PA28&lpg=PA28|passage=Item that the Wever whiche shall have the wevyng of eny wollen yerne to be '''webbed''' into cloth shall weve werk{{...}}|footer=[paraphrase] Likewise, that the weaver who is to weave any woollen yarn to be '''woven''' into cloth shall weave it well.<!-- not 100% sure about the meaning of "werk" here -->}}
